# Crosswalk

Every QSKOS class has a superclass in each standard that applies to it. The links are `rdfs:subClassOf` statements in `ontology/qskos.ttl`; the exported data does not repeat them.

## To DCAT 3

| QSKOS class | DCAT class | Path to the root |
|---|---|---|
| `qskos:Catalog` | `dcat:Catalog` | `qskos:Catalog` → `dcat:Catalog` → `dcat:Dataset` → `dcat:Resource` |
| `qskos:Dataset` | `dcat:Dataset` | `qskos:Dataset` → `dcat:Dataset` → `dcat:Resource` |
| `qskos:Distribution` | `dcat:Distribution` | `qskos:Distribution` → `dcat:Distribution` |

Properties: `dcat:dataset` (Catalog to Dataset), `dcat:distribution` (Dataset to Distribution), `dcat:mediaType`, `dcat:version`, and from Dublin Core terms `dct:title`, `dct:description`, `dct:creator`, `dct:license`, `dct:issued`, `dct:hasPart` (layers), `dct:requires` (vocabulary schemes), `dct:subject` (mapped objects), `dct:conformsTo` (this ontology).

### Properties

| QSKOS-side property | CRM property | How | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `oa:hasTarget` | `crm:P140_assigned_attribute_to` | CONSTRUCT rule Q3 | The annotation's target is the feature that receives the attribute. |
| `oa:hasBody` | `crm:P141_assigned` | CONSTRUCT rule Q3 | The value concept that is assigned. |
| `qskos:attribute` | `crm:P177_assigned_property_of_type` | rdfs:subPropertyOf (ontology) | The field concept says which kind of property is assigned. |
| `dct:creator` | `crm:P14_carried_out_by` | CONSTRUCT rule Q5 | Who made the annotation. |
| `dct:created` | `crm:P4_has_time-span / E52 Time-Span / P82_at_some_time_within` | CONSTRUCT rule Q5 | When the annotation was made (export time). |
| `dct:hasPart (Dataset to FeatureLayer)` | `crm:P106_is_composed_of` | documentation only | Both sides are E73 Information Object. Not materialised. |
| `dct:subject (Dataset to MappedObject)` | `crm:P67_refers_to` | documentation only | Not materialised. |
| `crm:P157_is_at_rest_relative_to (Feature to MappedObject)` | `itself` | written directly | The only CRM property that the export writes itself, because it places the E53 Place on the object. |
| `geo:hasGeometry, rdfs:member, dcat:distribution` | `no CRM property` | none | GeoSPARQL and DCAT structure with no CRM counterpart; CRM does not need to see it. |

## Decisions and pitfalls

### Why the crosswalk lives only in the ontology

Exports stay small and readable: they use `qskos:` classes. Anyone who needs the CIDOC CRM, DCAT, GeoSPARQL or Web Annotation view loads `ontology/qskos.ttl` into the same store and entails `rdfs:subClassOf` (RDFS). SPARQLing Unicorn reads properties (`geo:hasGeometry`, `geo:asWKT`, `rdfs:member`), not classes, and needs no entailment.

### Feature is an E53 Place, not an E26 Physical Feature

A QSKOS feature is a region on a 2D derivative of the object, positioned relative to it (`crm:P157`). Typing it E26 would say that the polygon *is* the damage.

### No CRMgeo SP6 on Feature

In CRMgeo 1.2, SP6 Declarative Place is also a subclass of `geo:Geometry`; `geo:Feature` and `geo:Geometry` are disjoint in GeoSPARQL, so both together would be inconsistent under a reasoner.

### Local coordinate systems

`qskos:LocalCoordinateSystem` is a CRMgeo SP4 (itself an E29 Design or Procedure). The link `qskos:inCoordinateSystem` is a candidate for alignment with `crmgeo:Q9_is_expressed_in_terms_of` once SP5 is settled.

### Bridges between foreign properties are rules, not axioms

The ontology asserts `subClassOf` / `subPropertyOf` only for its own terms. Mapping `oa:hasTarget` to `crm:P140` would assert something about a W3C property from outside; it is therefore a SPARQL CONSTRUCT rule in `ontology/queries.rq`.

### Open points

The ontology namespace `http://archaeology.link/ontology/qskos#` is a placeholder; a w3id.org IRI would be persistent. The CRMgeo parents are checked against CRMgeo 1.2 and should be re-checked against the CRMbase 7.1.x harmonised release.
